requirements.evidence: The contract is largely present: Entity/EntityMembership/UserRole with relations and scopes (app/Models/Entity.php:40-54, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:41-78, app/Models/UserRole.php:5-18), policies (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:11-34, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:11-33), factories, named routes and lang keys (routes/web.php:22-32, lang/en/ui.php:45-49, lang/pt_BR/ui.php:45-49), docs (docs/database-schema.md). However, registering ResolveCurrentEntity as a Livewire persistent middleware (app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:44) can intercept guest and zero-entity onboarding update requests before CreateEntity::submit() runs (app/Livewire/Entity/CreateEntity.php:28), and HomeController prefers a session entity over the specified 0/1/>1 dispatch (app/Http/Controllers/HomeController.php:20-25).

conventions.evidence: Uses #[Validate] + $this->validate() (app/Livewire/Entity/CreateEntity.php:25,32), server-side policies/gates (EntityController.php:43, Dashboard.php:19, CreateEntity.php:30), generated reversible migrations, deliberate #[Fillable] attributes, existing Blade components/Bulma layouts, and keeps docs in sync; it deviates by performing the entity-creation domain write inline in the Livewire component instead of an app/Actions class (app/Livewire/Entity/CreateEntity.php:28-70).

security.evidence: Authorization and validation are present on the actions (Gate::authorize('view') in app/Http/Controllers/EntityController.php:43, $this->authorize('view') in app/Livewire/Entity/Dashboard.php:19, $this->authorize('create') plus #[Validate] in CreateEntity.php:30-32), input is escaped with {{ }} and the dashboard entity is #[Locked]; but app/Http/Middleware/ResolveCurrentEntity.php:24-39 assumes a non-null user and is registered as a Livewire persistent middleware (app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:44), and the session tenant can differ from the requested dashboard entity (ResolveCurrentEntity.php:39-43 vs Dashboard.php:17-19).

tests.evidence: Broad Pest coverage exists: policies (tests/Feature/EntityDataModelTest.php:1287-1349), data-model constraints (EntityDataModelTest.php:1202-1265), routes/guests/verification (tests/Feature/EntityTenantTest.php:1386-1415), /home dispatch, tenant middleware, pick, switcher, dashboard 403/tamper, onboarding validation, slug retry/exhaustion and rate limiting; missing an HTTP-level test for the persistent middleware on guest/onboarding updates (the only test just asserts registration, EntityTenantTest.php:1513-1515), and the dashboard tamper assertion uses broad Exception::class (EntityTenantTest.php:1618-1624).

simplicity.evidence: The change reuses existing layouts/components, policies, factories and migrations and keeps methods small and direct; it duplicates isOwnerOrAdmin() in both policies (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:36-38, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:30-32) and adds a separate session-honoring branch in HomeController rather than reusing the middleware dispatch.

readability.evidence: Clear names and docblocks throughout (app/Tenancy/CurrentEntity.php:10-17, app/Http/Middleware/ResolveCurrentEntity.php:11-17, app/Livewire/Entity/CreateEntity.php:72-77), small focused methods (CurrentEntity is 68 lines, the middleware 47), consistent with sibling Laravel/Livewire style, and no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the task: models/migrations/policies/factories, tenancy, controllers, Livewire components, views, routes, lang, tests and the required docs updates (CHANGELOG.md, docs/database-schema.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/business-rules.md); no out-of-scope member/settings pages or unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: Registering ResolveCurrentEntity as a Livewire persistent middleware makes it run on every /livewire/update request, but it assumes $request->user() is non-null and calls CurrentEntity::dispatch() when the session is empty, so guest updates (login/register) throw a TypeError and a zero-entity user's onboarding submit is redirected before CreateEntity::submit() runs.

`/home` first honors an existing session entity, so a user with several memberships and a valid session is sent to that dashboard instead of entity.switcher, which is not the membership-count dispatch the task specifies.

The middleware always builds the tenant context from session('current_entity_id') while the dashboard binds and authorizes the requested {entity}, so a member can render /e/b under tenant a; no tenant-scoped query is made here yet, but the context and the page can disagree.

The only persistent-middleware test asserts that the class is registered; no test sends a guest or zero-entity Livewire update through the real HTTP route, so the middleware regression above is not caught.

The entity-and-owner transaction, slug generation and audit log are a domain write implemented inline in the Livewire component, whereas project convention routes domain writes through app/Actions/* (e.g. CreateQueue).
isOwnerOrAdmin() is duplicated in both policies, so the role matrix can drift; a shared helper would remove the copy-paste.

The tamper test expects the broad Exception::class and assigns an integer to a typed Entity property, which can produce a TypeError or unrelated failure instead of proving the #[Locked] guard; assert the specific Livewire locked-property exception.

review.summary: The change implements the entity/membership data model, policies, tenant session, onboarding, switcher and dashboard, and covers the task's contract with a substantial Pest test suite. It is close, but ResolveCurrentEntity is registered as a global Livewire persistent middleware without an unauthenticated/onboarding guard, so guest and zero-entity update requests can be redirected or fail before the component action runs; a few smaller issues remain around /home dispatch, tenant/route entity consistency, and the inline domain write.
